qt: to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (ID) Subject:

There is no doubt that it is now vital to ensure the competitiveness and sustainability of the European space industry in the face of international competition, particularly from the US, China and Russia. However, in a recent Financial Times article1, Josef Aschbacher, head of the European Space Agency (ESA), stated that there was ‘no guarantee’ that France’s ArianeGroup would continue to be Europe’s rocket launch company of choice, after the ESA agreed to introduce more competition to the market. 1.
How will the Commission support ArianeGroup and ensure that Europe is at the forefront of the space sector?
How will it help ArianeGroup and other European actors in the space sector to keep their strategic position, foster innovation and maintain independent access to space?

How does it intend to work with Member States, the ESA and industrial stakeholders to develop a coordinated strategy that promotes Europe’s sovereignty in the space industry, stimulates research and development, and ensures sustainable use of space for the benefit of the EU as a whole?
at: (English version) to the Commission Mathilde Androuët (ID) (1 February 2024) Subject: Sustainability of ArianeGroup in the ESA’s European space strategy There is no doubt that it is now vital to ensure the competitiveness and sustainability of the European space industry in the face of international competition, particularly from the US, China and Russia. However, in a recent Financial Times article (1), Josef Aschbacher, head of the European Space Agency (ESA), stated that there was ‘no guarantee’ that France’s ArianeGroup would continue to be Europe’s rocket launch company of choice, after the ESA agreed to introduce more competition to the market. 1.
How will the Commission support ArianeGroup and ensure that Europe is at the forefront of the space sector?

2. How will it help ArianeGroup and other European actors in the space sector to keep their strategic position, foster innovation and maintain independent access to space? 3. How does it intend to work with Member States, the ESA and industrial stakeholders to develop a coordinated strategy that promotes Europe’s sovereignty in the space industry, stimulates research and development, and ensures sustainable use of space for the benefit of the EU as a whole? (23 April 2024) In line with the EU Space Programme Regulation (2) to achieve the objectives of freedom of action, independence and security, it is essential that the EU benefits from an autonomous, secure and cost-effective capability to access space. In accordance with Article 5 of the EU Space Programme Regulation, the Commission supports the procurement and aggregation of launch services for the needs of the programme and, at their request, aggregation for Member States and international organisations. For the launch of EU satellites for the needs of the EU’s space flagships, the Commission gives priority to EU launch service providers from the territory of a Member State. Without prejudice to measures taken by the Member States or the European Space Agency, and within the available budgets, the Commission also supports the adaptations and developments of launch systems and infrastructures. For example, Horizon Europe (3) provides funding to research and innovation activities in the access to the space domain, including for high-thrust propulsion, reusability, new space transportation solutions or modern ground infrastructure. The Commission is working, in coordination with Member States and the European Space Agency, to ensure that the EU regains autonomous access to space. The upcoming EU Space Law will in particular address the question of a safe, secure and sustainable use of space.
